violated_contract:
A policy that authorizes an effect from the current user turn must match against the user's typed text, never against a machine-composed envelope that embeds it. The desktop runtime prefixes every run input with a clock preamble ("# Current Time
<iso> (<tz>)

"), and the explicit-memory-save intent matchers recognized a remember/save command only at the start of the prompt or after [.!?,;] punctuation — so a typed "remember that my favorite color is red" arrived behind the preamble's closing ')' and blank line, failed every command pattern, and was rejected with memory_save_not_authorized before any Swift or backend execution. The gate stayed fail-closed for the wrong reason: the authority evidence was present in the turn but invisible to a matcher anchored on the wrong string. Any gate that consumes a runtime-assembled prompt inherits this failure mode whenever the assembly prefix changes shape.
canonical_prevention: At the entry of every intent or authority predicate that consumes a run input, strip the known machine-generated preamble — exactly that prefix and nothing else, so any other leading text is still treated as user text — in both the Node policy and its Swift lockstep twin, then run the fail-closed guards (negation, question, passive mention, third-party command) on the raw turn. A preamble-only prompt with no user text must still reject. Keep the exact preamble reproduction plus preamble-prefixed negative, question, third-party, and bare-preamble cases in the shared intent corpus consumed by both suites, so neither implementation can accept the envelope as authority or drift apart on it.
